title: MLflow Assistant transcript leaked between users sharing a browser origin
answers: assistant chat history shows previous user's messages after sign-in
MLflow Assistant conversation visible to another user on same browser
assistant transcript persists across user logout and login
cross-user chat leak in the Assistant panel localStorage
body:
Symptom: After user A signs out and user B signs in on the same browser, the Assistant panel shows A's conversation.
Root cause: mlflow/server/js/src/assistant/AssistantContext.tsx:AssistantProvider persisted the transcript under one fixed key (CHAT_STORAGE_KEY_BASE) via useLocalStorage, which is not scoped to a user.
Fix pattern: Derive chatStorageKey as `${CHAT_STORAGE_KEY_BASE}.${username}` from useCurrentUserQuery; use the base key only when there is no username (auth off). Read and write that key with getLocalStorageItem/setLocalStorageItem, because useLocalStorage reads its key once and cannot follow an identity change.
Constraints: Auth-off local operator must keep the base key (no behavior change). Do not seed or persist while the current user query is still loading.
applies: Any change to the Assistant chat persistence or to per-user client state stored in localStorage in mlflow/server/js/src/assistant.
says: The assistant panel displays the previous user's chat history after switching accounts.
Signing in as another user still shows the earlier person's assistant messages.
Clear or isolate the assistant conversation history when a different account logs in.
Assistant chat transcripts persist in the browser across user logout and login.
search: In mlflow/server/js/src/assistant/AssistantContext.tsx:AssistantProvider, chat persistence must derive chatStorageKey as `${CHAT_STORAGE_KEY_BASE}.${username}` from useCurrentUserQuery and access it via getLocalStorageItem and setLocalStorageItem. When authentication is off, it uses CHAT_STORAGE_KEY_BASE, and it must not seed or persist while useCurrentUserQuery is loading. useLocalStorage is avoided because it reads its key only once and fails to follow identity changes.
